text:
sarah: FYI found an exported DB snapshot in an external vendor bucket. looks like it was copied overnight by an automated job. tagging the thread so security + storage can triage.

rafael: thanks. bucket name and object path? any kms key info?

sarah: s3://vendor-ingest-uploads/redwood/alpha-2026-03-21.sql.gz. CloudTrail shows CopyObject at 2026-03-21T01:03:12Z by role `backup-agent@ec2`. KMS key logged as arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/plat-0a1b2c. no tenant-cmk header present.

priya: if a platform CMK was used that's a policy failure for tenant separation. we need to stop further copies, preserve evidence, and remove write perms for that agent pending investigation.

nate: agree. short-term actions: 1) quarantine the copied object (copy to an internal quarantine bucket), 2) apply a bucket policy deny for that object prefix, 3) disable the backup-agent's ability to use the platform key (revoke grant).

encops-bot: Alert: S3Copy detected. source: redwood-prod-snapshots, dest: vendor-ingest-uploads, principal: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/backup-agent, kms_key: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/plat-0a1b2c. Incident created INC-2026-042.

rafael: can we determine whether the copy request included s3:ObjectTagging indicating tenant=alpha? if not, that's more evidence of automation misconfig. also check whether the upload used multipart or single put.

sarah: no tenant tag on the dest object. it only has upload-agent=backup-agent. multipart=false.

priya: I'll run the KMS steps. run `aws kms list-grants --key-id plat-0a1b2c --region us-west-2` and revoke any grants associated with the backup-agent role. if revocation reveals wide usage, warn storage team about potential restore breakage.

nate: I'll put the policy deny in place for redwood-exports and vendor-ingest-uploads for s3:PutObject for the backup-agent principal. snippet for IAM policy (inline deny):

```
{
  "Effect": "Deny",
  "Action": "s3:PutObject",
  "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::vendor-ingest-uploads/redwood/*",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/backup-agent"}
}
```

rafael: we should avoid a blanket deny that breaks legitimate restores. prefer a conditional deny requiring either s3:RequestObjectTag/tenant equals principal tag or encryption context to contain tenant-id. add a short TTL so ops can revert if needed.

sarah: preserving exported object now with `aws s3 cp s3://vendor-ingest-uploads/redwood/alpha-2026-03-21.sql.gz s3://redwood-quarantine/INC-2026-042/ --metadata-directive REPLACE --metadata investigation=true`.

priya: after revoking grants, we may need to rotate the platform key if it was broadly used for tenant data. but rotating will impact restores for all snapshots encrypted under that key. plan: inventory snapshots using plat-0a1b2c, coordinate rewrap strategy (re-encrypt exported copies with tenant CMKs or a wrap key).

nate: filing RBAC change request: add condition to backup-agent role to remove kms:Encrypt on platform key and add explicit kms:GenerateDataKey only under a per-tenant role. also propose adding org SCP that enforces per-tenant CMK usage for cross-account snapshot exports.

encops-bot: Triage update: Severity P2. Tasks assigned: sarah(preserve object), priya(revoke kms grants + key inventory), nate(temporary deny + RBAC change request), rafael(cloudtrail audit + automation owner contact).

rafael: CloudTrail shows assume-role from ec2 instance i-0abc123 at 2026-03-21T01:02:58Z then CopyObject at 01:03:12Z. i'm reaching out to the automation owners on #backup-automation.

sarah: thanks. i'll follow up once quarantine copy completes. keep me posted before any key rotation. :thumbsup:
